record.narrative: No validation evidence arrived and no validation requests remain, so this synthesis is discovery-only and uses 95 percent Welch intervals for discovery claims while interpreting validation intervals independently. I updated the accepted set by moving several positive claims to unresolved when their lower bound was below the 0.15 composite dependency-score threshold, even when the point estimate exceeded threshold. This separates threshold-supported associations from directional context-dependent associations. Direction convention: for direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is negative, so exposed has more negative outcome_001 and stronger composite dependency; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the raw contrast is positive and exposed has weaker dependency. Robust dataset-only main associations: feature_027=1 stronger dependency, feature_037=1 stronger dependency, feature_002=1 weaker dependency, and feature_010=1 weaker dependency. All have discovery and validation estimates and lower bounds far above threshold, and the many subgroup acceptances reflect persistence rather than proof of interaction. feature_063 is context-dependent and not uniformly threshold precise overall: overall H27 is now unresolved because the validated lower bound is below threshold, but several contexts are threshold-supported, especially the clean core-negative population feature_002=0/feature_037=0/feature_010=0/feature_027=0 (H213) and selected numeric strata or combinations (H161 high feature_040, H214 low feature_030, H225 high feature_053, H233 high feature_040, H234 high feature_051, H236 high feature_053 and high feature_051, H237 high feature_040 and high feature_051, H245 high feature_053 and high feature_040). feature_003 remains a narrow positive signal, not a broad predictor; it is unresolved in contexts such as H95, H215, H222, H231, H240 and is rejected as a threshold claim in high feature_030 contexts and interaction tests. Negative or null findings: constructed binary markers feature_007, feature_058, and feature_015 show no threshold main effects or supported signature interactions; feature_017 is null after validation; feature_047 is null and numerically redundant with feature_021; feature_031 and most categorical contrasts are subthreshold; feature_060 is null overall; the main interaction tests for feature_002 by feature_010, feature_002 or feature_010 by feature_053, feature_063 by feature_040 or feature_051, and feature_003 by feature_030 or feature_063 are unsupported. Residual uncertainty is mainly whether feature_063 high-numeric threshold effects are true effect modification or selected additive contexts, and whether small-cell combinations or untested categorical levels change that conclusion. The most informative next analysis is the set of feature_063 interaction tests registered here within the clean core-negative eligibility, using high feature_053, high feature_040, and high feature_051 as modifiers. These use four valid cells when available and directly test whether the threshold high-stratum feature_063 contrasts differ from the complementary feature_063 contrasts in the same eligible population. All conclusions are associations in this dataset only; none support causality, biological mechanism, coding-level interpretation, single-gene knockout meaning, or generalizability.

prompt:
Iteration 20/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- outcome_001: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent validation is exhausted, so this explore step registers discovery-only refinements that are most likely to improve inference about the two remaining ambiguous predictors, feature_063 and feature_003. Direction convention: for direction -1 mean or interaction claims, a positive signed estimate corresponds to a raw negative exposed-minus-comparator contrast, meaning more negative outcome_001 and stronger composite dependency. A threshold claim will be accepted only if the signed 95 percent Welch lower bound exceeds 0.15 composite dependency-score units; positive intervals with lower bounds below 0.15 will be treated as directional/context-dependent only. The first three proposals follow the clean core-negative population feature_002=0, feature_037=0, feature_010=0, feature_027=0, where the feature_063 association has been threshold supported and where several high numeric contexts were also threshold supported. They test whether high numeric contexts are genuinely additive or whether each is only a proxy for the other. Specifically, H233 accepted feature_063 in high feature_040, H234 accepted it in high feature_051, H225 accepted it in high feature_053, and H236/H237 accepted high-high combinations. The new interaction tests ask, within high feature_040, whether feature_063 is more negative when feature_053 is high; within high feature_051, whether feature_063 is more negative when feature_040 is high; and within high feature_053, whether feature_063 is more negative when feature_051 is high. Expected direction is negative raw interaction, corresponding to a positive signed estimate under direction -1, because accepted high-high effects were larger than several single-high-context effects. Plausible alternatives are null or attenuated effect modification. These interactions use accepted split cells with exposed complement cells expected to remain above 20, though the controller will enforce cell counts. The last two proposals address feature_003, which remains narrow and not clearly broad. Prior core-negative feature_063-negative feature_003 estimates were positive but threshold borderline. If high feature_053 is informative, feature_003 may become threshold in that context; otherwise it remains a weak directional marker. These analyses are dataset-only associations and do not support causal, biological, coding-level, single-gene-knockout, or generalizability claims. Priority is to analyze active H247 and H249 plus these paired-context feature_063 interactions, then the feature_003 high-feature_053 comparisons if analysis capacity remains.

prompt:
Iteration 20/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence

prompt:
Iteration 20/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- outcome_001: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative:
No independent validation budget remains, so all due results are assessed as discovery-only 95% Welch intervals with explicit caution for multiplicity and post-hoc selection. Direction convention is as stated: for direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate corresponds to the claimed stronger-dependency pattern (raw exposed-minus-comparator negative), and I do not re-sign intervals.

The new feature_063 paired-context interaction tests do not establish a new threshold-supported effect-modification claim in the clean core-negative eligibility population. H247 (feature_053>=10 modifier, signed +0.086 [-0.076, 0.248]) and H249 (feature_051>=2.6735 modifier, signed +0.104 [-0.053, 0.260]) are positive but far below the 0.15-unit threshold and cross zero. H250 (feature_053 modifier within high feature_040, signed +0.168 [-0.056, 0.393]) has a point estimate above threshold but the lower bound is negative and the interval includes zero. H251 (feature_040 modifier within high feature_051, signed +0.268 [0.047, 0.489]) is the most suggestive: it excludes zero and has a point estimate above threshold, but its lower bound is well below 0.15 and the contrast is small-sample and post-hoc. H252 (feature_051 modifier within high feature_053, signed +0.121 [-0.078, 0.320]) is below threshold and crosses zero. These are kept unresolved and deferred because they may represent weak, context-dependent interaction signals, but none meet the threshold criterion of a signed lower bound exceeding 0.15. They do not justify stronger claims of feature_063 effect modification, especially after repeated high-stratum selection and overlapping feature_040/feature_051/feature_053 contexts.

The feature_003 results remain narrow and subthreshold. H253 (feature_003 within core-negative, feature_063=0, feature_053>=10) is positive but below threshold (+0.115 [0.045, 0.185]), so I keep it unresolved and close it as a weak directional context rather than a meaningful association. H254 (feature_053>=10 interaction for feature_003 in the same eligible population) is signed negative (-0.124 [-0.242, -0.007]), i.e. it is in the opposite direction from the claimed stronger-dependency interaction and excludes zero in that opposite direction; this does not support the H254 claim, so I reject it and close it. H93 (feature_003 among feature_002=0, signed +0.142 [0.064, 0.221]) is positive but below threshold, so it remains a weak unresolved directional signal. H94 (feature_003 among feature_002=1, signed +0.039 [-0.112, 0.190]) is essentially null, so it is rejected.

The categorical contrasts are also null or unsupported. H165 (rare feature_059 level_002 vs level_003, signed -0.023 [-0.300, 0.253]) is not in the claimed direction and is too wide to support a threshold claim. H166 (feature_061 level_001 vs level_002, signed +0.057 [-0.024, 0.138]) and H167 (feature_061 level_003 vs level_002, signed -0.007 [-0.150, 0.137]) are near zero, with H166's upper bound below threshold and H167 mixed. record.narrative: No new validation arrived and no validation budget remains, so this synthesis is a dataset-only final report using the stated 0.15 composite dependency-score threshold rule. The robust threshold-supported associations are: feature_027=1 is associated with stronger composite dependency, H128 discovery +0.792 [0.676,0.907] and validation +0.836 [0.672,1.001]; feature_037=1 is associated with stronger composite dependency, H24 discovery +0.833 [0.767,0.898] and validation +0.795 [0.695,0.896]; feature_002=1 is associated with weaker dependency in the claimed direction, H63 discovery +0.832 [0.766,0.897] and validation +0.783 [0.688,0.878]; and feature_010=1 is associated with weaker dependency, H37 discovery +0.423 [0.327,0.520] and validation +0.471 [0.334,0.607]. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is negative, so exposed has more negative outcome_001 and stronger dependency; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means exposed has weaker dependency. All four main findings have lower bounds far above threshold and are accepted in many subgroup contrasts, but most direct interaction tests involving these variables were null, so the subgroup acceptances indicate persistence of the main associations rather than proof of effect modification. The main unresolved predictor is feature_063. Its overall effect is not threshold-precise because H27 is validated at +0.248 [0.109,0.388], with the lower bound below threshold, so the overall main effect remains unresolved. However, feature_063 has threshold-supported mean-difference contrasts in selected contexts, especially the clean core-negative population feature_002=0, feature_037=0, feature_010=0, feature_027=0, where H213 is +0.260 [0.182,0.338], and in high numeric contexts including high feature_053, H225 +0.295 [0.194,0.395], high feature_040, H233 +0.321 [0.210,0.431], high feature_051, H234 +0.311 [0.197,0.426], and high-high combinations such as H236, H237, and H245. These accepted feature_063 contexts are numerous and overlapping, so they should be described as context-dependent, post-hoc selected associations rather than a uniform main effect. The interaction tests do not establish a threshold-supported modifier: H247 is +0.086 [-0.076,0.248], H249 is +0.104 [-0.053,0.260], H250 is +0.168 [-0.056,0.393], H252 is +0.121 [-0.078,0.320], and even the most suggestive H251 is +0.268 [0.047,0.489] with a lower bound far below threshold. The most informative next analysis is therefore a single pre-specified high-high context interaction in the core-negative population, combining high feature_053 and high feature_040. This registered proposal asks whether the accepted high-context feature_063 contrasts represent genuine effect modification or selected additive contexts. Feature_003 remains weak and below threshold: H93 is +0.142 [0.064,0.221], H95 validated is +0.151 [0.056,0.246], and H253 is +0.115 [0.045,0.185]; it is not a threshold predictor and its interactions are unsupported. Negative findings include no threshold main effects for the constructed binary markers feature_007, feature_058, or feature_015 and no supported interactions with feature_038, feature_018, or feature_036; feature_017 is null after validation; feature_047 is null and numerically redundant with feature_021; feature_031 and most other binary features are subthreshold or null; feature_060 is null; and feature_024, feature_046, feature_052, feature_054, feature_059, and feature_061 categorical contrasts do not support threshold associations. Key negative interaction findings include rejected feature_002 by feature_010 after validation, rejected feature_063 by feature_040 or feature_051 interactions in several contexts, and rejected feature_003 interaction claims. These conclusions are associations in this dataset only and do not establish causality, biological mechanism, coding-level meaning, single-gene knockout interpretation, or external generalizability.

prompt:
Iteration 21/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- outcome_001: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No assessments are due and the independent validation budget is exhausted, so the remaining work is discovery-only refinement of the principal ambiguity in the accepted evidence: whether feature_063 represents a uniform predictor or a context-dependent marker with genuine effect modification. The robust accepted predictors remain feature_027, feature_037, feature_002, and feature_010; feature_003 remains weakly directional and subthreshold; the constructed research markers and signatures have not supported threshold associations. Direction convention: for a direction -1 claim, a positive signed estimate means the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is negative, i.e. feature_063=1 is associated with more negative outcome_001 and stronger composite dependency. For interactions, the raw interaction is the comparison inside the subgroup minus the comparison in the complement within the same eligible population. A negative raw interaction means the feature_063 stronger-dependency association is larger in the high numeric stratum than outside it, giving a positive signed estimate under direction -1. Acceptance will require a signed 95% Welch lower bound above 0.15 composite dependency-score units in the claimed direction. I prioritize the already active but still untested H255, because it directly tests whether the accepted high feature_053/high feature_040 mean-difference context reflects amplification of feature_063 association relative with the rest of the core-negative population. I repeat that comparison only to keep it at the front of the analysis queue and preserve its active unresolved status. I then register reverse paired-context interactions: feature_053 modification among high feature_051 cells, feature_051 modification among high feature_040 cells, and feature_040 modification among high feature_053 cells. These complement the earlier paired interaction tests and ask whether any one numeric stratum genuinely amplifies the feature_063 association when the other is fixed. Finally, I register complement mean differences for high feature_040 without high feature_053, high feature_051 without high feature_040, and high feature_053 without high feature_051. These tests assess whether feature_063 remains associated in single-high contexts, which would support additive context selection, versus being concentrated in high-high combinations. The interactions anticipate a negative raw interaction if the accepted high-high effects are more than context selection; the complement mean differences are expected attenuated or null if high-high interactions were driven by overlap or selection. Plausible alternatives include attenuated point estimates, wide small-sample intervals, or complete nulls, especially because many contexts were discovered post hoc and overlap substantially. If no new signed lower bound exceeds 0.15, I will conclude that feature_063 remains a selected-context mean association without threshold-supported effect modification. These analyses support dataset-only associations only; they do not establish causality, biological mechanism, coding-level interpretation, single-gene-knockout meaning, or external generalizability.

prompt:
Iteration 21/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- outcome_001: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. Iteration 21/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- outcome_001: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

prompt:
Iteration 21/25, stage appraise, attempt 2.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- outcome_001: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: No independent validation budget remains, so all due claims are evaluated as discovery-stage 95% Welch intervals and are interpreted only as associations in the supplied dataset. The acceptance rule is unchanged: accept only when the signed lower bound exceeds 0.15 composite dependency-score units in the claimed direction. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is negative, i.e. exposed exposure is associated with more negative outcome_001 and stronger composite dependency. I do not re-sign estimates. None of the newly delivered due results meets the threshold rule, and no new accepted claim is added. The feature_063 interaction block remains context-dependent and subthreshold. H255 is the strongest new paired high-context interaction, signed +0.188 [0.018, 0.358]. It excludes zero and has a point estimate above threshold, but the lower bound is far below 0.15, the exposed subgroup cells are small, and the high-high context was selected after many overlapping post-hoc tests. I therefore mark it unresolved and closed rather than accept it. H258 is similar: signed +0.232 [0.016, 0.448], positive and credible but not threshold-supported; unresolved closed. H257 is signed +0.109 [-0.130, 0.349], below threshold and null-inclusive; reject closed. H262 is signed +0.193 [-0.004, 0.390]; although the point estimate is suggestive, the interval includes zero and the lower bound is far below threshold, so the claimed interaction is not supported; reject closed. The single-high complement mean-difference tests are informative for additivity versus true modification. H259 gives +0.223 [0.046, 0.400] and H261 gives +0.231 [0.091, 0.371], both directionally consistent with feature_063=1 associated with stronger dependency but below threshold in their lower bounds. They support selected-context or additive association rather than a new threshold-supported mean effect; unresolved closed. H260 gives +0.160 [-0.005, 0.325], essentially null-inclusive; reject closed. The marker/signature interaction tests are uniformly noninformative for biologically meaningful effect modification. H13 is +0.065 [-0.066, 0.196], H14 is -0.001 [-0.135, 0.132], H15 is +0.085 [-0.046, 0.216], H16 is -0.058 [-0.192, 0.076], and H17 is +0.016 [-0.116, 0.147]; all are null-inclusive, below threshold, or in the opposite direction, so all are rejected and closed. I deliberately restrict assessments to the due claims and do not duplicate assessments for canonical duplicate cards. These conclusions are dataset-only associations; they do not support causality, biological mechanism, coding-level interpretation, single-gene-knockout meaning, or external generalizability.

prompt:
Iteration 21/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_001 (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (feature_038, feature_018, feature_036) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (feature_007, feature_058, feature_015) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains

{"narrative": "No due assessments or validation response deadlines were present, and no new validation could be requested because the validation budget is exhausted. The final synthesis therefore relies on the ledger evidence and applies the same rule used throughout: accept a claim as scientifically meaningful only when the signed 95% Welch lower bound exceeds 0.15 composite dependency-score units in the claimed direction. For direction -1, positive signed estimates mean the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is negative, i.e. more negative outcome_001 and stronger composite dependency; for direction +1, positive signed estimates mean more positive outcome_001 and weaker dependency. Estimates are interpreted as returned, with no re-signing.

Supported findings. Four opaque binary predictors have robust threshold-supported main associations in this dataset. feature_027=1 vs 0 is associated with stronger dependency: H128 discovery R101 signed +0.792 [0.676, 0.907] and independent validation R104 signed +0.836 [0.672, 1.001]. feature_037=1 vs 0 is associated with stronger dependency: H24 discovery R17 signed +0.833 [0.767, 0.898] and validation R38 signed +0.795 [0.695, 0.896]. feature_002=1 vs 0 is associated with weaker dependency, i.e. higher outcome_001: H63 discovery R48 signed +0.832 [0.766, 0.897] and validation R64 signed +0.783 [0.688, 0.878]. feature_010=1 vs 0 is associated with weaker dependency: H37 discovery R18 signed +0.423 [0.327, 0.520] and validation R51 signed +0.471 [0.334, 0.607]. These are dataset-level associations, not causal effects. Their effect sizes are large relative to the outcome spread and are supported by validated independent intervals where available.

The accepted subgroup results for these four predictors are numerous, but the direct interaction tests involving them are mostly null or below threshold. For example, the proposed feature_002 by feature_010 interaction was positive in discovery H113 R85 +0.210 [0.019, 0.400] but failed independent validation R91 +0.023 [-0.325, 0.370]; feature_002 by feature_037 H119 R92 +0.023 [-0.121, 0.167] was rejected; and feature_010 by feature_037 H120 R93 +0.032 [-0.196, 0.260] was rejected. Similar null or subthreshold interaction results were observed for feature_027, feature_040, feature_051 and feature_053 modifiers. Therefore the safest interpretation is that the accepted subgroup acceptances show persistence of the main associations across many measured strata, not strong evidence for effect modification.

feature_063 is the main unresolved predictor. Its overall main effect remains unresolved: H27 direction -1 discovery R20 signed +0.227 [0.131, 0.323] and validation R25 signed +0.248 [0.109, 0.388]. The point estimates are directionally consistent with feature_063=1 associated with stronger dependency, but the validated lower bound is below 0.15, so the overall effect cannot be accepted as threshold-supported. By contrast, feature_063 has threshold-supported mean differences in selected contexts, especially in the clean core-negative population defined by feature_002=0, feature_037=0, feature_010=0 and feature_027=0: H213 R198 signed +0.260 [0.182, 0.338]. It also shows accepted threshold-supported contrasts in high numeric contexts: high feature_053 H225 R218 +0.295 [0.194, 0.395], high feature_040 H233 R226 +0.321 [0.210, 0.431], and high feature_051 H234 R227 +0.311 [0.197, 0.426]. Overlapping high-high contexts are also accepted: H236 R229 +0.352 [0.206, 0.498], H237 R230 +0.428 [0.275, 0.581], and H245 R238 +0.391 [0.246, 0.536]. These accepted contrasts are strongly direction consistent, but because the contexts were selected after extensive post-hoc comparison and overlap substantially, they should be described as context-dependent selected associations rather than a uniform main effect of feature_063.

The interaction tests for feature_063 do not yet establish a threshold-supported modifier. The most suggestive paired high-context interaction H255 remains unresolved: R253 signed +0.188 [0.018, 0.358]. H258 is similarly unresolved: R255 signed +0.232 [0.016, 0.448]. Several others are null or opposite-inclusive: H257 R254 +0.109 [-0.130, 0.349] rejected, H262 R259 +0.193 [-0.004, 0.390] rejected, and earlier core-negative interactions H247 R241 +0.086 [-0.076, 0.248], H249 R242 +0.104 [-0.053, 0.260], H250 R243 +0.168 [-0.056, 0.393] and H252 R245 +0.121 [-0.078, 0.320] are below threshold or include zero. Complement mean-difference tests favor selected or additive high-context associations rather than clean amplification: H259 R256 +0.223 [0.046, 0.400] and H261 R258 +0.231 [0.091, 0.371] are directionally positive but below threshold; H260 R257 +0.160 [-0.005, 0.325] is rejected. Thus the evidence supports a context-dependent feature_063 mean association, with genuine modification remaining possible but not demonstrated.

Negative findings. The constructed binary research markers feature_007, feature_058 and feature_015 show no threshold main effects: H1 R1, H2 R2 and H3 R3 are near-null and closed. Their tested interactions with constructed standardized signatures feature_038, feature_018 and feature_036 are also unsupported: H4 R4, H5 R5, H6 R6 and later H13 R260, H14 R261, H15 R262, H16 R263, H17 R264 are null, subthreshold or opposite direction. record.narrative:
No due assessments or validation response deadlines were present, and no new validation could be requested because the validation budget is exhausted. The final synthesis therefore relies on the ledger evidence and applies the same rule used throughout: accept a claim as scientifically meaningful only when the signed 95% Welch lower bound exceeds 0.15 composite dependency-score units in the claimed direction. For direction -1, positive signed estimates mean the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is negative, i.e. more negative outcome_001 and stronger composite dependency; for direction +1, positive signed estimates mean more positive outcome_001 and weaker dependency. Estimates are interpreted as returned, with no re-signing.

Supported findings. Four opaque binary predictors have robust threshold-supported main associations in this dataset. feature_027=1 vs 0 is associated with stronger dependency: H128 discovery R101 signed +0.792 [0.676, 0.907] and independent validation R104 signed +0.836 [0.672, 1.001]. feature_037=1 vs 0 is associated with stronger dependency: H24 discovery R17 signed +0.833 [0.767, 0.898] and validation R38 signed +0.795 [0.695, 0.896]. feature_002=1 vs 0 is associated with weaker dependency, i.e. higher outcome_001: H63 discovery R48 signed +0.832 [0.766, 0.897] and validation R64 signed +0.783 [0.688, 0.878]. feature_010=1 vs 0 is associated with weaker dependency: H37 discovery R18 signed +0.423 [0.327, 0.520] and validation R51 signed +0.471 [0.334, 0.607]. These are dataset-level associations, not causal effects. Their effect sizes are large relative to the outcome spread and are supported by validated independent intervals where available.

The accepted subgroup results for these four predictors are numerous, but the direct interaction tests involving them are mostly null or below threshold. For example, the proposed feature_002 by feature_010 interaction was positive in discovery H113 R85 +0.210 [0.019, 0.400] but failed independent validation R91 +0.023 [-0.325, 0.370]; feature_002 by feature_037 H119 R92 +0.023 [-0.121, 0.167] was rejected; and feature_010 by feature_037 H120 R93 +0.032 [-0.196, 0.260] was rejected. Similar null or subthreshold interaction results were observed for feature_027, feature_040, feature_051 and feature_053 modifiers. Therefore the safest interpretation is that the accepted subgroup acceptances show persistence of the main associations across many measured strata, not strong evidence for effect modification.

feature_063 is the main unresolved predictor. Its overall main effect remains unresolved: H27 direction -1 discovery R20 signed +0.227 [0.131, 0.323] and validation R25 signed +0.248 [0.109, 0.388]. The point estimates are directionally consistent with feature_063=1 associated with stronger dependency, but the validated lower bound is below 0.15, so the overall effect cannot be accepted as threshold-supported. By contrast, feature_063 has threshold-supported mean differences in selected contexts, especially in the clean core-negative population defined by feature_002=0, feature_037=0, feature_010=0 and feature_027=0: H213 R198 signed +0.260 [0.182, 0.338]. It also shows accepted threshold-supported contrasts in high numeric contexts: high feature_053 H225 R218 +0.295 [0.194, 0.395], high feature_040 H233 R226 +0.321 [0.210, 0.431], and high feature_051 H234 R227 +0.311 [0.197, 0.426]. Overlapping high-high contexts are also accepted: H236 R229 +0.352 [0.206, 0.498], H237 R230 +0.428 [0.275, 0.581], and H245 R238 +0.391 [0.246, 0.536]. These accepted contrasts are strongly direction consistent, but because the contexts were selected after extensive post-hoc comparison and overlap substantially, they should be described as context-dependent selected associations rather than a uniform main effect of feature_063.

The interaction tests for feature_063 do not yet establish a threshold-supported modifier. The most suggestive paired high-context interaction H255 remains unresolved: R253 signed +0.188 [0.018, 0.358]. H258 is similarly unresolved: R255 signed +0.232 [0.016, 0.448]. Several others are null or opposite-inclusive: H257 R254 +0.109 [-0.130, 0.349] rejected, H262 R259 +0.193 [-0.004, 0.390] rejected, and earlier core-negative interactions H247 R241 +0.086 [-0.076, 0.248], H249 R242 +0.104 [-0.053, 0.260], H250 R243 +0.168 [-0.056, 0.393] and H252 R245 +0.121 [-0.078, 0.320] are below threshold or include zero. Thus the evidence supports a context-dependent feature_063 mean association, with genuine modification remaining possible but not demonstrated.

Negative findings. The constructed binary research markers feature_007, feature_058 and feature_015 show no threshold main effects: H1 R1, H2 R2 and H3 R3 are near-null and closed.
